title: Deep Learning of Phase Transitions for Bilinear-Biquadratic Spin-1 Chains from Correlation Aspects
title_zh: 从相关性角度深度学习双线性双二次自旋 1 链的相变
summary: 我们使用我们之前开发的无标签机器学习管道 citeMing21、Ming23 研究了不同相关函数在重建 spin-1 双线性双二次链相图中的作用，通过双线性和双二次耦合之间的角度 θ 进行参数化，其中自动编码器将 iDMRG 相关矩阵压缩为潜在特征，并通过轮廓分析进行 K 均值聚类将它们分组为相。
abstract: arXiv:2610.19995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the role of different correlation functions in reconstructing the phase diagram of the spin-1 bilinear-biquadratic chain, parametrized by the angle θ between the bilinear and biquadratic couplings, using our previously developed label-free machine-learning pipeline citeMing21, Ming23, in which an autoencoder compresses iDMRG correlation matrices into latent features and K-means clustering with silhouette analysis groups them into phases. Without any prior labels, the scheme reveals four natural phases, the Haldane, dimerized, critical trimerized, and ferromagnetic phases, and accurately locates the Takhtajan-Babujian (θ=-π/4), SU(3)-symmetric Uimin-Lai-Sutherland (θ=π/4), and Ferro-Dimer (θ=5π/4) transition points; a shallow supervised refinement further sharpens the phase boundaries. We find that different correlation functions play fundamentally different roles in phase identification. The SU(3)-symmetric correlation alone selects a four-cluster partition that can be associated with the four phases, whereas the spin-spin and dimer-dimer correlations must be combined to recover the complete phase diagram. In contrast, the trimer-trimer correlation behaves as a marginal correlation: it is insufficient for phase identification by itself but improves the precision of the predicted phase boundaries when combined with the other correlations. Furthermore, the latent representations and silhouette values reveal signatures that we relate to the θ dependence of the correlations within each phase and, tentatively, to the underlying renormalization-group structure. These results demonstrate that machine learning can not only identify quantum phases but also uncover the physical information encoded in different correlation functions.

title: ActMOF: Mapping Reticular Synthesis through Active Learning
title_zh: ActMOF：通过主动学习绘制网状综合
summary: 网状化学允许从其构建单元设计金属有机框架（MOF），但其合成仍然受到实验数据稀疏、结晶结果嘈杂以及缺乏比较主动学习策略的基准的限制。虽然贝叶斯优化 (BO) 等数据驱动方法可以提高合成成功率，但预先选择合适的优化器来绘制 MOF 结晶图谱在很大程度上仍然是凭经验得出的。在这里，我们提出 ActMOF，一个基于实验的基准，用于比较羧酸铝 MOF 合成中的搜索策略。 ActMOF 是通过实验测量的微波合成来模拟的，每个编码条件都分配了一个基于衍射峰强度和半峰全宽计算的结晶度指数。
abstract: arXiv:2610.19404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reticular chemistry allows metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) to be designed from their building units, yet their synthesis remains constrained by sparse experimental data, noisy crystallization outcomes, and the absence of benchmarks for comparing active-learning strategies. While data-driven approaches such as Bayesian optimization (BO) can improve synthesis success rates, selecting appropriate optimizers beforehand for mapping MOF crystallization landscapes remains largely empirical. Here we present ActMOF, an experiment-grounded benchmark for comparing search strategies in aluminum-carboxylate MOF synthesis. ActMOF is emulated from experimentally measured microwave syntheses with each encoded condition assigned a crystallinity index calculated based on diffraction peak intensity and full width at half-maximum. By benchmarking policies guided by Gaussian processes (GP), tree ensembles and large language models (LLM), ActMOF placed the GP family among the leading policies for active learning in sparse synthesis landscapes. It then demonstrated transferability by guiding the microwave synthesis of six reticularly related aluminum MOFs. All six campaigns gave crystalline products within a fixed budget of 12 experiments each, and established a reusable testbed for AI-driven MOF synthesis.

title: Inferring Transition-Dipoles from Two-Dimensional Infrared Spectroscopy with Deep Learning
title_zh: 文献研究：Inferring Transition-Dipoles from Two-Dimensional Infrared Spectroscopy with Deep Learning
summary: Two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy is a powerful nonlinear technique for probing vibrational couplings, anharmonicities, coherence, and molecular dynamics. Among the microscopic parameters…
abstract: arXiv:2610.19972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy is a powerful nonlinear technique for probing vibrational couplings, anharmonicities, coherence, and molecular dynamics. Among the microscopic parameters encoded in 2D IR spectra, transition dipoles are fundamental quantities that characterize molecular structure and govern light-matter interactions. However, reconstructing these quantities from spectroscopic data remains a challenging inverse problem. Here, we introduce a physics-informed convolutional neural network (CNN), Spec2DipoleNet, trained on 2D IR spectra generated via the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian (NHH) method. This multi-task CNN reconstructs the transition dipole matrices under physically-motivated masking constraints. On the validation set, the model achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.085, an R² of 0.97, and a normalized cross-correlation of 0.98. It reliably recovers matrix elements associated with allowed transitions, while larger deviations are observed for nominally forbidden transitions. Our results suggest that transition dipole operators can be quantitatively inferred from 2D IR spectra, highlighting the potential of physics-informed deep learning for extracting microscopic quantum parameters from multidimensional spectroscopic data.

title: Tracking large chemical reaction networks and rare events by neural networks
title_zh: 文献研究：Tracking large chemical reaction networks and rare events by neural networks
summary: Chemical reaction networks are widely used to model stochastic dynamics in biophysical processes. Their exact probabilistic description via the chemical master equation becomes intractable for high-di…
abstract: arXiv:2512.10309v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Chemical reaction networks are widely used to model stochastic dynamics in biophysical processes. Their exact probabilistic description via the chemical master equation becomes intractable for high-dimensional systems due to the exponential growth of the state space. This difficulty is further exacerbated when metastable transitions and rare events dominate the dynamics. Here, we present an advanced neural-network approach that effectively tackles large reaction networks and rare-event dynamics within a unified framework. Building on autoregressive representations of the full joint probability distribution, we achieve efficient training through second-order optimization methods, including natural gradient descent and the time-dependent variational principle. We leverage enhanced-sampling strategies that enable accurate resolution of low-probability regions governing rare transitions. We demonstrate the method on a multistable genetic toggle switch and a mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascade consisting of 16 species and 35 reactions with dense coupling. We further quantify rare events in spatially extended Schlögl models in both one- and two-dimensional lattices, reaching system sizes with extremely large state spaces up to 3×10¹⁵. These results highlight the potential of neural modeling as a flexible and scalable framework for studying high-dimensional chemical reaction networks and rare events.

title: TorchSpin: Differentiable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Simulation in PyTorch
title_zh: 文献研究：TorchSpin: Differentiable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Simulation in PyTorch
summary: Interpreting electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra commonly requires repeated forward simulation and optimization of spin Hamiltonian parameters. Established software provides mature simulatio…
abstract: arXiv:2610.18924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interpreting electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra commonly requires repeated forward simulation and optimization of spin Hamiltonian parameters. Established software provides mature simulation and fitting methods, but these calculations are not generally available as differentiable components within machine-learning workflows. We present TorchSpin, an open-source PyTorch framework that ports the organization and numerical conventions of EasySpin into a tensor-based computational environment. Representative calculations spanning continuous-wave EPR, ENDOR, pulse EPR, spin dynamics, trajectory simulation, and magnetometry closely reproduced corresponding EasySpin results. In matched benchmarks, TorchSpin CPU execution was faster than EasySpin for six of nine workloads although performance depended strongly on the calculation. We therefore focused on the capabilities enabled by automatic differentiation in PyTorch. In a Cu(II) powder-spectrum demonstration, feedback propagated through TorchSpin improved the quality of a supervised convolutional neural network (CNN) without using parameter labels during refinement. Models trained from randomly initialized CNNs using only noisy spectra and TorchSpin reconstruction loss achieved median similarities of ≥ 0.99. CNNs trained on TorchSpin-generated libraries also transferred without adaptation to independently generated EasySpin spectra with performance comparable to EasySpin-trained controls. Once trained, the CNN produced initial parameter estimates in approximately 1 ms per spectrum while a batch of 512 was processed in approximately 1.3 ms with GPU acceleration. TorchSpin therefore provides both a tested Python implementation of established EPR calculations and a differentiable physical layer for rapid learned inference, spectral refinement, and parameter-label-free training.

title: Neural-Network Solutions to Real-Space Charge Density and Generalization
title_zh: 文献研究：Neural-Network Solutions to Real-Space Charge Density and Generalization
summary: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem establishes that, in principle, the ground state (GS) charge density contains all GS information of a many-electron system, such that all GS observables can be expressed as…
abstract: arXiv:2609.14906v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem establishes that, in principle, the ground state (GS) charge density contains all GS information of a many-electron system, such that all GS observables can be expressed as functionals of the GS charge density. Conventional Kohn-Sham density functional theory requires iterative solution of the self-consistent-field equations at substantial computational cost, motivating the development of deep learning surrogates for electronic structure calculations and, in turn, accelerating computer-aided materials design. Here, we propose AIDEN, an Atomic-Interaction Density Equivariant Network for solving real-space charge density. AIDEN separates the element-dependent one-center density from environment-induced density redistribution and represents the latter through complementary atom- and edge-centered tensor correlations. A continuous low-rank Gaussian decoder then reconstructs the density at arbitrary spatial coordinates while reusing atomic encodings independently of the evaluation grid. AIDEN achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on periodic crystal benchmarks while remaining competitive for molecular systems, and further demonstrates zero-shot transferability across several structurally distinct out-of-distribution case studies. Furthermore, AIDEN provides substantially faster inference than both baseline models and full SCF calculations, enabling efficient charge density reconstruction for large-scale electronic structure calculations.

title: Risk-Controlled DFT Selection for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
title_zh: 文献研究：Risk-Controlled DFT Selection for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
summary: Automated materials discovery requires evaluating large pools of candidate configurations, with density functional theory (DFT) as a major throughput bottleneck. Pretrained machine-learned interatomic…
abstract: arXiv:2610.19630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated materials discovery requires evaluating large pools of candidate configurations, with density functional theory (DFT) as a major throughput bottleneck. Pretrained machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approximate DFT cheaply, but their errors vary by orders of magnitude across configurations, making it difficult to decide when to trust the MLIP predictions and when to fall back to DFT. We frame this decision as a risk-controlled selection problem and solve it within a conformal risk control (CRC) framework. Each configuration is mapped from atomic numbers and Cartesian coordinates to a fixed geometric descriptor, which a lightweight predictor uses to estimate an MLIP-DFT disagreement score in energy, average force, and maximum force. CRC then calibrates this score into a selection threshold for DFT labeling such that the MLIP error on the unselected configurations, which keep their MLIP labels, stays below a user-chosen fraction α of the expected error. Under an identical guarantee across eight dataset-MLIP pairs, our predictor routes 7% and 14% fewer configurations to DFT at α=0.3 than committee baselines. Because committee disagreement overlooks errors the MLIPs share, our gains are largest when the DFT labels and MLIP training data differ in DFT functional and basis set, and narrow when the two agree. Without model access, the structure-only predictor also ranks errors as well as the target MLIP's latent representation and outperforms widely used descriptors such as Smooth Overlap of Atomic Positions (SOAP) and Atom-Centered Symmetry Functions (ACSF).

title: Fluctuation-driven multi-step charge density wave melting in monolayer TiSe₂
title_zh: 单层TiSe ₂中波动驱动的多步电荷密度波熔化
summary: TiSe ₂中电荷密度波（ CDW ）相的确切微观起源、对称性和热熔融机制仍然存在激烈争论，特别是关于手性结构顺序和多步相变。利用由精确的机器学习原子间势驱动的大规模分子动力学，我们解决了单层TiSe ₂的有限温度结构动力学。我们证明， CDW熔化偏离了传统的均值场二阶行为，经历了两步过程，其特征是具有增殖畴壁的扩展波动区（ 200-250 K ）、相位退相干、组分选择性熔化和过阻尼的软光学声子。此外，各向异性长波长热波动自发稳定具有P1对称性的不对称3Q CDW级。
abstract: arXiv:2604.20355v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The exact microscopic origin, symmetry, and thermal melting mechanism of the charge density wave (CDW) phase in TiSe₂ remain intensely debated, particularly regarding chiral structural order and multi-step phase transitions. Using large-scale molecular dynamics driven by an accurate machine-learning interatomic potential, we resolve the finite-temperature structural dynamics of the monolayer TiSe₂. We demonstrate that CDW melting deviates from conventional mean-field second-order behavior, undergoing a two-step process characterized by an extended fluctuation region (200-250 K) with proliferating domain walls, phase decoherence, component-selective melting, and an overdamped soft optical phonon. Furthermore, anisotropic long-wavelength thermal fluctuations spontaneously stabilize an asymmetric 3Q CDW order with P1 symmetry. These findings provide a unified microscopic framework for fluctuation-driven transitions in 2D quantum materials, demonstrating that the complex CDW physics of TiSe₂ is captured entirely via non-perturbative electron-phonon and phonon-phonon interactions.

title: Non-Abelian quantum Hall states at strong Landau level mixing: finding anyons with first-principles AI
title_zh: 非阿贝尔量子霍尔在强朗道水平混合状态：使用第一原理AI寻找任意子
summary: 非阿贝尔任意子，即构成容错拓扑量子计算基础的奇异粒子，预计将在偶分母填充因子下以分数量子霍尔态出现。确定实现了哪种拓扑顺序已被证明是一个具有挑战性的问题，需要对逼真的朗道水平混合进行准确的、非扰动的处理，迄今为止理论研究中一直缺少这种处理。在这里，我们提出了非阿贝尔量子霍尔问题的第一个完整解，其中包括所有电子和所有朗道能级，用于填充因子ν = 3/2的自旋极化电子。
abstract: arXiv:2610.18967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Abelian anyons, strange particles forming the basis of fault-tolerant topological quantum computing, are predicted to emerge in fractional quantum Hall states at even-denominator filling factors. Identifying which topological order is realized has proven to be a challenging problem that requires an accurate, non-perturbative treatment of realistic Landau level mixing, which has so far been missing from theoretical studies. Here we present the first complete solution of non-Abelian quantum Hall problem that includes all electrons and all Landau levels, for spin-polarized electrons at filling factor ν = 3/2. We develop a momentum-resolved neural-network variational wave function, optimized solely on the microscopic Hamiltonian, which gives direct access to the topologically degenerate ground states. Without any physics input about the expected outcome, it discovers a degenerate ground-state manifold whose entanglement reveals anyons with quantum dimension sqrt2, the hallmark of Ising-type non-Abelian order. By directly computing the overlap with trial wave functions, we further show that Landau level mixing favors the anti-Pfaffian over other candidate states. Our results demonstrate the power of neural-network wave functions in finding and characterizing non-Abelian anyons from first principles, in regimes of strong Landau level mixing, relevant to many recent experiments.

title: Cavity-tunable Pseudospin-Hall Topology and Edge Transport
title_zh: 文献研究：Cavity-tunable Pseudospin-Hall Topology and Edge Transport
summary: Topological edge states are a hallmark of topological phases, with their existence tied to bulk band topology through bulk-edge correspondence. In photonic pseudospin-Hall systems, these states exhibi…
abstract: arXiv:2610.20343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological edge states are a hallmark of topological phases, with their existence tied to bulk band topology through bulk-edge correspondence. In photonic pseudospin-Hall systems, these states exhibit pseudospin-momentum locking, with lattice interactions and interface geometry determining each pseudospin's propagation direction. Reversing the pseudospin-dependent propagation direction without altering the lattice configuration or excitation handedness remains a fundamental challenge in controlling topological edge transport. Here, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate cavity-tunable topological edge transport in a microwave metasurface embedded within a metallic cavity. Varying the cavity height reshapes resonator interactions, driving band inversion and topological phase transition while preserving the lattice geometry. For a fixed domain-wall configuration, this transition reverses the propagation direction associated with each pseudospin while preserving pseudospin-momentum locking. Excitations with the same handedness are observed to launch edge waves propagating in opposite directions at their respective edge-band frequencies determined by the cavity height. These results establish cavity electrodynamics as an external means of controlling the bulk topology and reconfiguring the directional response of topological interfaces, creating new opportunities for topological wave routing in fixed photonic lattice structures.

title: Revealing the Spatial Distribution of Dust and Plasma Solitary Waves in Jupiter's Innermost Magnetosphere Using Juno Waves Observations
title_zh: 文献研究：Revealing the Spatial Distribution of Dust and Plasma Solitary Waves in Jupiter's Innermost Magnetosphere Using Juno Waves Observations
summary: Jupiter's faint ring system contains micron- and submicron-sized dust whose dynamics are influenced by the planet's rapidly rotating magnetic field. Optical observations have established the morpholog…
abstract: arXiv:2610.20541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Jupiter's faint ring system contains micron- and submicron-sized dust whose dynamics are influenced by the planet's rapidly rotating magnetic field. Optical observations have established the morphology of the main ring and halo, but tenuous dust close to Jupiter remains difficult to characterize. We analyze nearly a decade of in-situ Juno Waves electric-field measurements using a two-stage convolutional neural network to identify and classify dust impacts, solitary waves, and other plasma waves. These in-situ dust-impact detections reveal a radially evolving structure extending well inside the traditionally observed halo. In the innermost region, dust is concentrated in a compact, equatorially symmetric layer, indicating that the optical inner boundary does not mark the end of the dust population. Farther outward, the layer expands vertically into a broad halo before contracting toward the main ring, directly revealing the toroidal morphology of the Jovian halo. Dust number density is enhanced within the halo and near the main-ring--halo transition. The vertical distribution also develops hemispheric asymmetries that vary with radial distance, consistent with an influence of Jupiter's magnetic geometry on charged-dust dynamics. In contrast, solitary waves occur predominantly at high latitudes, and their mapped magnetic footprints show a strong spatial correspondence with Jovian auroral structures, particularly the main auroral oval. Together, these in-situ measurements extend the remote-sensing picture of Jupiter's rings and reveal previously unresolved dust and plasma structures in its innermost magnetosphere.

title: Beyond Kitaev exchange: Γ'-driven magnetism in Ag₃LiRh₂O₆
title_zh: 超越基塔耶夫交换：Ag₃LiRh2O₆ 中 γ' 驱动的磁性
summary: 在基塔耶夫磁体中，挫折来自于键依赖性自旋各向异性相互作用，这有可能实现备受追捧的量子自旋液相。然而，以基塔耶夫交换为主的材料实现很少，并且扩展基塔耶夫模型的广泛参数空间在很大程度上仍未通过实验进行探索。在这里，我们使用密度泛函理论、簇多体、自旋波和密度矩阵重正化计算来表明，最近发现的蜂窝状铑酸盐Ag₃LiRh2O₆具有非对角线交换Ђ'，其数量级仅次于铁磁Kitaev交换K₁。
abstract: arXiv:2610.19770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Kitaev magnets, frustration arises from bond-dependent spin anisotropic interactions, which can potentially realize sought-after quantum spin liquid phases. However, material realizations with dominating Kitaev exchange are scarce and the broad parameter space of extended Kitaev models remains largely unexplored experimentally. Here, we use density-functional theory, cluster many-body, spin-wave, and density-matrix renormalization calculations to show that the recently discovered honeycomb rhodate Ag₃LiRh₂O₆ hosts an off-diagonal exchange Γ₁' that is second in magnitude only to the ferromagnetic Kitaev exchange K₁. This combination of K₁ and Γ₁' explains key experimental observations, an unusually high magnetic ordering temperature of 94 K at ambient pressure and its rapid decrease under hydrostatic pressure as Ag₃LiRh₂O₆ evolves from ferromagnetic toward zigzag order within the honeycomb planes. Our spin-wave calculations further predict an unusual topology of the magnon bands arising from the Γ₁' term in the spin Hamiltonian of the honeycomb layer. We show that the large trigonal splitting of t₂g states enhances Γ₁', the hitherto underappreciated term in Kitaev magnets, and opens the way to new interesting regimes of the extended Kitaev model.

title: Ab initio study of magnetic Cu 2 Sb compounds related to antiferromagnetic CuMnAs
title_zh: 文献研究：Ab initio study of magnetic Cu 2 Sb compounds related to antiferromagnetic CuMnAs
summary: The antiferromagnetic metal CuMnAs has become a workhorse of antiferromagnetic spintronics. A broad range of phenomena has been demonstrated in this material, most notably current-induced switching an…
abstract: The antiferromagnetic metal CuMnAs has become a workhorse of antiferromagnetic spintronics. A broad range of phenomena has been demonstrated in this material, most notably current-induced switching and heat-driven quench switching, both first realized in CuMnAs. CuMnAs belongs to a much larger family of intermetallic compounds sharing the tetragonal Cu2Sb-type structure, yet the magnetic properties of most of its members, and their potential for spintronics, have not been studied. Here we report a systematic density functional theory (DFT) study of the magnetic and electronic structure of more than 50 compounds of this family, intended to guide future theoretical and experimental work toward spintronic applications. We find a wide range of magnetic ground states, among them over 20 new antiferromagnetic candidates.

title: Designing Hamiltonians with Exactly Flat Higher-Vortexable Bands
title_zh: 设计具有精确平坦的高涡能带的哈密顿量
summary: 阿哈罗诺夫-卡舍尔哈密顿量的零模在任何非均匀磁场中形成完全平坦的可涡旋陈氏带，类似于最低的朗道能级。我们询问哪些本地哈密顿主义者拥有完全平坦的高涡旋能带。对于标量哈密顿量，精确平坦的第一可涡带需要与局部场成比例的质量；狄拉克类似物具有相同的结构。对于具有非零平均通量的周期性伯纳尔双层石墨烯，当且仅当层间跳跃具有非零均值时，精确的零模对才是真正可第一涡旋的；相反，零均值跳跃给出了可分解的对。多轨道模型产生任意阶的精确高涡链，同时保持一阶动量。
abstract: arXiv:2610.20380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The zero modes of the Aharonov-Casher Hamiltonian form an exactly flat, vortexable Chern band in any nonuniform magnetic field, analogous to the lowest Landau level. We ask which local Hamiltonians host exactly flat higher-vortexable bands. For a scalar Hamiltonian, an exactly flat first-vortexable band requires a mass proportional to the local field; the Dirac analogue has the same structure. For periodic Bernal bilayer graphene with nonzero mean flux, the exact zero-mode pair is genuinely first-vortexable if and only if the interlayer hopping has nonzero mean; zero-mean hopping instead gives a decomposable pair. Multiorbital models yield exact higher-vortexable chains to arbitrary order, while remaining first order in momentum.
